records.literal_gloss: Many for are called, few but chosen.

en.L: For many are called, but few [are] chosen."
en.B: For the invited are many, but the chosen are few."
en.R: God invites many people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses only a few."

es.L: Porque muchos son invitados, pero pocos [son] elegidos».
es.B: Porque los invitados son muchos, pero los elegidos son pocos».
es.R: Dios invita a mucha gente, pero elige solo a unos pocos».

fr.L: Car beaucoup sont appelés, mais peu [sont] choisis. »
fr.B: Car les invités sont nombreux, mais les élus sont peu nombreux. »
fr.R: Dieu invite beaucoup de gens, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’en choisit que quelques-uns. »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa wengi ni walioalikwa, lakini wachache [ni] waliochaguliwa."
sw.B: Kwa maana walioalikwa ni wengi, lakini waliochaguliwa ni wachache."
sw.R: Mungu anawaalika watu wengi, lakini anawachagua wachache tu."

vi.L: Vì có nhiều người được gọi, nhưng ít người được chọn."
vi.B: Vì người được mời thì nhiều, nhưng người được chọn thì ít."
vi.R: Vì Đức Chúa Trời mời nhiều người, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chỉ chọn một số ít."

ko.L: 부름받은 사람은 많으나, 택함받은 사람은 적기 때문이다."
ko.B: 초대받은 사람은 많지만, 택함받은 사람은 적다."
ko.R: 하나님께서는 많은 사람을 부르시지만, 그 가운데 적은 사람만 택하신다."

pt.L: Pois muitos são chamados, mas poucos [são] escolhidos."
pt.B: Pois os convidados são muitos, mas os escolhidos são poucos."
pt.R: Deus convida muitas pessoas, mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} escolhe só algumas."

am.L: ብዙዎች ተጠርተዋልና፣ የተመረጡት ግን ጥቂቶች ናቸው።»
am.B: የተጠሩት ብዙዎች፣ የተመረጡት ግን ጥቂቶች ናቸውና።»
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ብዙ ሰዎችን ይጋብዛል፤ የሚመርጠው ግን ጥቂቶችን ብቻ ነው።»

ru.L: Ведь много званых, мало же избранных.»
ru.B: Ведь приглашённых много, а избранных мало.»
ru.R: Бог приглашает многих людей, но выбирает {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} только немногих.»

hi.L: क्योंकि बुलाए हुए बहुत हैं, पर चुने हुए थोड़े।"
hi.B: क्योंकि बुलाए गए तो बहुत हैं, पर चुने गए थोड़े हैं।"
hi.R: परमेश्वर बहुत लोगों को बुलाते हैं, पर वे थोड़े ही लोगों को चुनते हैं।"

uk.L: Бо багато покликаних, а мало вибраних.»
uk.B: Бо запрошених багато, а вибраних мало.»
uk.R: Бог запрошує багатьох людей, але {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} вибирає лише небагатьох.»

ja.L: なぜなら、招かれる者は多いが、選ばれる者は少ないからである。」
ja.B: 招かれる者は多いが、選ばれる者は少ない。」
ja.R: 神は多くの人を招かれる。けれども、神が選ばれるのは、ほんの少しの人だけだ。」

decisions.choice: called: invited
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "invited" in 22:3-9. Many receive the king's invitation.

decisions.choice: chosen: those whom God accepts at the feast
decisions.reason: The saying sums up the parable. Many were invited, yet the first guests refused and one guest was thrown out. The chosen are those who come and are found fit, by God's choice.

decisions.choice: God invites; he chooses
alternatives: many are called, few are chosen
decisions.reason: The passive words imply that God is the one who calls and chooses. Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the invited are many, the chosen are few
alternatives: many are invited, few are chosen
decisions.reason: Balanced sets the two groups side by side as the Greek does, with the numbers last for emphasis.

decisions.choice: invitados
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the guests "invited" in verses 3, 4 and 8 (meaning decision m1). "Invitados" keeps the saying tied to the story; "llamados" would lose the link.

decisions.choice: walioalikwa
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the guests "invited" in verses 3, 4 and 8 (meaning decision m1). "Walioalikwa" keeps the saying tied to the story; "walioitwa" would lose the link.

decisions.choice: "부름받은" (L), "초대받은" (B); "택함받은" (L, B); God named at Readable
decisions.reason: The word is the same as the invited guests of the story (meaning decision); Balanced says "초대받은" to keep that link, and Readable names God as the one who calls, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "được gọi" (L); "được mời" (B); "Đức Chúa Trời mời" (R) for "called"; "được chọn"
decisions.reason: "Called" here means invited (meaning decision), which ties the saying to the feast; Literal keeps the Greek verb "gọi" and Balanced the sense "mời". Readable names God as the one who invites and chooses, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; the honorific "बुलाते हैं", "वे ... चुनते हैं" for God
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for God and Jesus comes from the honorific plural at every level, as the style guide says, in this whole passage.

decisions.choice: "神は……招かれる", "神が選ばれる" (R)
decisions.reason: The passive words imply that God calls and chooses (m2); Readable says so, as the English Readable does, with the honorific form for God in Jesus' words.

source.text: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Then having gone, the Pharisees took counsel how him they might trap in a word.

en.L: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in [what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said].
en.B: Then the Pharisees went off and plotted how they could catch Jesus out by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own words.
en.R: Then the Pharisees went away and made plans. They wanted to trick Jesus into saying something wrong.

es.L: Entonces los fariseos fueron y tomaron consejo sobre cómo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atraparían en [lo que dijera].
es.B: Entonces los fariseos se retiraron y tramaron cómo hacer caer a Jesús con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} propias palabras.
es.R: Entonces los fariseos se fueron e hicieron planes. Querían engañar a Jesús para que dijera algo indebido.

fr.L: Alors les Pharisiens, s’en étant allés, tinrent conseil pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} prendre au piège par [ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dirait].
fr.B: Alors les Pharisiens se retirèrent et se concertèrent pour trouver le moyen de piéger Jésus par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} propres paroles.
fr.R: Ensuite, les Pharisiens sont partis et ils ont fait des plans. Ils voulaient piéger Jésus en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} faisant dire quelque chose de mal.

sw.L: Kisha Mafarisayo, wakiondoka, walishauriana jinsi wangemnasa kwa neno [alilosema].
sw.B: Kisha Mafarisayo waliondoka, wakapanga njama jinsi ya kumkamata Yesu kwa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe.
sw.R: Kisha Mafarisayo waliondoka, wakapanga mpango. Walitaka kumdanganya Yesu ili aseme jambo baya.

vi.L: Bấy giờ những người Pha-ri-si đi ra và bàn mưu làm thế nào để gài bẫy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong lời nói.
vi.B: Bấy giờ những người Pha-ri-si đi ra và bàn mưu để bắt lỗi Đức Giê-xu bằng chính lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói.
vi.R: Rồi những người Pha-ri-si bỏ đi và bàn tính với nhau. Họ muốn lừa Đức Giê-xu để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói ra điều gì sai.

ko.L: 그때에 바리새파 사람들이 가서, 어떻게 하면 그분을 말로 올무에 걸리게 할까 의논하였다.
ko.B: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 물러가서, 어떻게 하면 예수를 말로 책잡을 수 있을까 의논했다.
ko.R: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 물러가서 계획을 세웠다. 그들은 예수께서 무엇인가 잘못된 말을 하시게 만들어서 꼬투리를 잡으려고 했다.

pt.L: Então os fariseus foram e combinaram como poderiam apanhá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} em [alguma coisa que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dissesse].
pt.B: Então os fariseus saíram e tramaram um jeito de apanhar Jesus nas {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} próprias palavras.
pt.R: Então os fariseus foram embora e fizeram planos. Eles queriam enganar Jesus para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dissesse alguma coisa errada.

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ ፈሪሳውያን ሄደው በቃሉ እንዴት እንደሚያጠምዱት ተማከሩ።
am.B: ከዚያም ፈሪሳውያን ሄደው ኢየሱስን በገዛ ቃሉ እንዴት እንደሚያጠምዱት ተመካከሩ።
am.R: ከዚያም ፈሪሳውያን ሄደው ዕቅድ አወጡ። ኢየሱስ ስሕተት የሆነ ነገር እንዲናገር ሊያታልሉት ፈለጉ።

ru.L: Тогда фарисеи, пойдя, совещались, как бы поймать {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} на слове.
ru.B: Тогда фарисеи ушли и стали совещаться, как бы поймать Иисуса на {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} собственных словах.
ru.R: Тогда фарисеи ушли и стали строить планы. Они хотели хитростью заставить Иисуса сказать что-нибудь неправильное.

hi.L: तब फ़रीसियों ने जाकर सलाह की कि [यीशु] को बात में कैसे फँसाएँ।
hi.B: तब फ़रीसी चले गए और षड्यंत्र रचने लगे कि यीशु को उन्हीं की बातों में कैसे फँसाएँ।
hi.R: तब फ़रीसी चले गए और उन्होंने योजना बनाई। वे चाहते थे कि यीशु से कोई ग़लत बात कहलवाकर उन्हें फँसा लें।

uk.L: Тоді фарисеї, пішовши, порадилися, як би {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} впіймати на слові.
uk.B: Тоді фарисеї відійшли і змовилися, як би підловити Ісуса на {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} ж словах.
uk.R: Тоді фарисеї пішли і почали радитися. Вони хотіли хитрістю змусити Ісуса сказати щось не те.

ja.L: そのとき、ファリサイ派の人々は出て行って、どのようにしてイエスを言葉でわなにかけようかと相談した。
ja.B: それから、ファリサイ派の人々は出て行って、イエスの言葉じりをとらえてわなにかけようと相談した。
ja.R: それから、ファリサイ派の人々は出て行って、相談しました。イエスに何かまちがったことを言わせて、わなにかけようとしたのです。

decisions.choice: trap: catch, as a hunter snares an animal
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a snare. They wanted a statement they could use against him.

decisions.choice: took counsel: made a plan together
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 12:14, when the Pharisees plot to destroy Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns, pronouns before the verb and possessives (lo, sus)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the end of the verb ("atraparlo", "muéstrenme"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens, les Hérodiens (L, B), capitalised; des partisans de la famille du roi Hérode (R, 22:16)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in Mark 12:13. Readable explains the Herodians as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, wewe)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("wangemnasa", "mnanijaribu"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This applies to the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "말로 올무에 걸리게 하다" (L); "말로 책잡다" (B); "꼬투리를 잡다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures snaring an animal (meaning decision); Literal keeps the snare, Balanced and Readable use the words of the Korean Mark 12:13.

decisions.choice: "gài bẫy" (L); "bắt lỗi" (B); "lừa" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a hunter's snare (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture, as in Mark 12:13, and Balanced and Readable say what they wanted.

decisions.choice: "впіймати на слові"
alternatives: "упіймати в пастку в [тому, що Він скаже]"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:13, the Ukrainian idiom says what the Greek says without the supplied words the English Literal needs.

decisions.choice: "わなにかける" (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a snare (m1). "わな" keeps the hunter's picture at every level; Balanced adds "言葉じりをとらえて" for "in a word", as in Mark 12:13.

source.text: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·

records.literal_gloss: And they send to him the disciples of them with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that true you are and the way of God in truth you teach, and not it is a care to you about no one, not for you look at face of men;

en.L: And they send their disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are true and teach the way of God in truth, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not care about anyone, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not look at [the] face of {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: They sent their own disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along with the Herodians. "Teacher," they said, "we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are truthful and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach God's way in keeping with the truth. No one's opinion moves {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not judge people by their rank.
en.R: They sent some of their followers to Jesus, together with some men who supported King Herod's family. They said, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are honest. We know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach the truth about the way God wants people to live. You are not afraid of anyone, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treat important people the same as everyone else.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} envían sus discípulos con los herodianos, diciendo: «Maestro, sabemos que eres veraz y enseñas el camino de Dios en verdad, y no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} importa nadie, pues no miras [el] rostro de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.B: Le enviaron sus discípulos junto con los herodianos. «Maestro», le dijeron, «sabemos que eres sincero y que enseñas el camino de Dios conforme a la verdad. La opinión de nadie {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hace cambiar, porque no juzgas a la gente por su rango.
es.R: Enviaron a algunos de sus seguidores a ver a Jesús, junto con unos hombres que apoyaban a la familia del rey Herodes. Le dijeron: «Maestro, sabemos que eres honesto. Sabemos que enseñas la verdad sobre cómo quiere Dios que viva la gente. No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} da miedo nadie, porque tratas a las personas importantes igual que a todos los demás.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoient leurs disciples avec les Hérodiens, disant : « Maître, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es vrai et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enseignes la voie de Dieu dans la vérité, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} soucies de personne, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne regardes pas au visage des {{gender:humains|hommes}}.
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoyèrent leurs propres disciples, accompagnés des Hérodiens. « Maître, dirent-ils, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dis la vérité et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enseignes la voie de Dieu en toute vérité. L’opinion de personne ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}influence, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne juges pas les gens d’après leur rang.
fr.R: Ils ont envoyé à Jésus quelques-uns de leurs disciples, avec des partisans de la famille du roi Hérode. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Maître, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es honnête. Nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enseignes la vérité sur la façon dont Dieu veut que les gens vivent. Tu n’as peur de personne, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} traites les gens importants comme tous les autres.

sw.L: Na wanawatuma {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} wanafunzi wao pamoja na wafuasi wa Herode, wakisema, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mkweli na unafundisha njia ya Mungu katika kweli, wala humjali mtu yeyote, kwa maana hutazami uso wa watu.
sw.B: Waliwatuma wanafunzi wao {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} pamoja na wafuasi wa Herode. Wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mtu wa kweli, na kwamba unafundisha njia ya Mungu kulingana na kweli. Maoni ya mtu yeyote hayakuyumbishi, kwa sababu huwapimi watu kwa vyeo vyao.
sw.R: Waliwatuma baadhi ya wafuasi wao kwa Yesu, pamoja na watu fulani walioiunga mkono familia ya Mfalme Herode. Wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwaminifu. Tunajua kwamba unafundisha ukweli kuhusu jinsi Mungu anavyotaka watu waishi. Humwogopi mtu yeyote, kwa sababu unawatendea watu wakubwa sawa na watu wengine wote.

vi.L: Và họ sai các môn đồ của mình cùng với những người thuộc phe Hê-rốt đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói rằng: "Thưa Thầy, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người chân thật và dạy đường lối của Đức Chúa Trời theo chân lý, và Thầy không nể ai cả, vì Thầy không nhìn mặt người ta.
vi.B: Họ sai các môn đồ của mình cùng với những người thuộc phe Hê-rốt đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người ngay thật và dạy đường lối của Đức Chúa Trời theo đúng chân lý. Thầy không để ai chi phối mình, vì Thầy không xét người theo địa vị.
vi.R: Họ sai mấy người môn đồ của mình cùng với mấy người ủng hộ gia đình vua Hê-rốt đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người thật thà. Thầy dạy sự thật về cách Đức Chúa Trời muốn người ta sống. Thầy không sợ ai cả, vì Thầy đối xử với người quan trọng cũng như với mọi người khác.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 자기 제자들을 헤롯 당원들과 함께 그분께 보내며 말한다. "선생님, 저희는 선생님께서 참되시고, 하나님의 길을 진리 안에서 가르치시며, 아무에게도 마음을 쓰지 않으신다는 것을 압니다. 선생님께서는 사람들의 얼굴을 보지 않으시기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그들은 자기 제자들을 헤롯 당원들과 함께 예수께 보냈다. 그들이 말했다. "선생님, 저희는 선생님께서 진실하신 분이시고, 하나님의 길을 참되게 가르치시며, 아무에게도 휘둘리지 않으신다는 것을 압니다. 선생님께서는 사람의 지위를 따지지 않으십니다.
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들은 자기 제자들을 예수께 보냈다. 헤롯 왕의 집안을 따르는 사람들도 함께 보냈다. 그들이 말했다. "선생님, 저희는 선생님께서 정직하신 분이라는 것을 압니다. 선생님께서는 하나님께서 원하시는 삶의 길을 참되게 가르치십니다. 선생님께서는 아무도 두려워하지 않으십니다. 높은 사람이든 낮은 사람이든 똑같이 대하십니다.

pt.L: E enviam a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os seus discípulos com os herodianos, dizendo: "Mestre, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és sincero e ensinas na verdade o caminho de Deus, e não {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preocupas com ninguém, pois não olhas para o rosto {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}}.
pt.B: Mandaram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os seus próprios discípulos, junto com os herodianos. "Mestre", disseram, "sabemos que és sincero e que ensinas o caminho de Deus de acordo com a verdade. A opinião dos outros não {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} influencia, porque não julgas as pessoas pela posição que ocupam.
pt.R: Eles mandaram alguns dos seus seguidores até Jesus, junto com alguns homens que apoiavam a família do rei Herodes. Eles disseram: "Mestre, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és honesto. Sabemos que ensinas a verdade sobre o jeito como Deus quer que as pessoas vivam. Tu não tens medo de ninguém, porque tratas as pessoas importantes do mesmo jeito que todas as outras.

am.L: ደቀ መዛሙርታቸውንም ከሄሮድስ ወገኖች ጋር ወደ እርሱ ይልካሉ፤ እንዲህም እያሉ፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ እውነተኛ እንደ ሆንህ፣ የእግዚአብሔርንም መንገድ በእውነት እንደምታስተምር፣ ለማንም ግድ እንደሌለህም እናውቃለን፤ የሰዎችን ፊት አትመለከትምና።
am.B: ደቀ መዛሙርታቸውን ከሄሮድስ ወገኖች ጋር ወደ እርሱ ላኩ። «መምህር ሆይ» አሉት፤ «አንተ እውነተኛ እንደ ሆንህና የእግዚአብሔርን መንገድ በእውነት እንደምታስተምር እናውቃለን። የማንም ሰው አስተያየት አያንቀሳቅስህም፤ ሰዎችን በማዕረጋቸው አታዳላምና።
am.R: ከዚያም ከደቀ መዛሙርታቸው አንዳንዶቹን የንጉሥ ሄሮድስን ቤተሰብ ከሚደግፉ ሰዎች ጋር ወደ ኢየሱስ ላኩ። እነርሱም እንዲህ አሉ፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ አንተ ሐቀኛ እንደ ሆንህ እናውቃለን። እግዚአብሔር ሰዎች እንዴት እንዲኖሩ እንደሚፈልግ እውነቱን እንደምታስተምርም እናውቃለን። ማንንም አትፈራም፤ ታላላቅ ሰዎችን እንደ ሌላው ሰው ታያለህና።

ru.L: И посылают к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} учеников своих с иродианами, говоря: «Учитель, мы знаем, что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} истинен и пути Божьему в истине учишь, и не заботишься ни о ком, ведь {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} не смотришь на лицо людей.
ru.B: Они послали к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} своих учеников вместе с иродианами. «Учитель», — сказали они, — «мы знаем, что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} правдив и что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} учишь пути Божьему в согласии с истиной. Ничьё мнение не сбивает {{deity_pronoun:тебя|Тебя}}, ведь {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} не судишь о людях по их положению.
ru.R: Они послали к Иисусу некоторых своих учеников вместе с людьми, которые поддерживали семью царя Ирода. Они сказали: «Учитель, мы знаем, что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} честный. Мы знаем, что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} учишь правде о том, как Бог хочет, чтобы жили люди. Ты никого не боишься, потому что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} относишься к важным людям так же, как ко всем остальным.

hi.L: और वे अपने चेलों को हेरोदियों के साथ उनके पास भेजते हैं, जो कहते हैं, "हे गुरु, हम जानते हैं कि आप सच्चे हैं और परमेश्वर का मार्ग सत्य से सिखाते हैं, और आपको किसी की परवाह नहीं, क्योंकि आप मनुष्यों का मुँह नहीं देखते।
hi.B: उन्होंने अपने चेलों को हेरोदियों के साथ उनके पास भेजा। "हे गुरु," उन्होंने कहा, "हम जानते हैं कि आप सच बोलते हैं और परमेश्वर का मार्ग सत्य के अनुसार सिखाते हैं। किसी की राय आपको डिगा नहीं सकती, क्योंकि आप लोगों को उनके पद से नहीं आँकते।
hi.R: उन्होंने अपने कुछ चेलों को कुछ ऐसे आदमियों के साथ यीशु के पास भेजा जो राजा हेरोदेस के परिवार के पक्ष में थे। उन्होंने कहा, "हे गुरु, हम जानते हैं कि आप ईमानदार हैं। हम जानते हैं कि आप सच-सच सिखाते हैं कि परमेश्वर लोगों से कैसा जीवन चाहते हैं। आप किसी से नहीं डरते, क्योंकि आप बड़े लोगों से भी वैसा ही बर्ताव करते हैं जैसा बाक़ी सबसे।

uk.L: І посилають до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} своїх учнів з іродіанами, кажучи: «Учителю, ми знаємо, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} правдивий і по правді навчаєш дороги Божої, і {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} ні на кого не зважаєш, бо {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} не дивишся на обличчя людей.
uk.B: Вони послали до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} своїх учнів разом з іродіанами. «Учителю», — сказали вони, — «ми знаємо, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} правдивий і навчаєш Божої дороги згідно з істиною. Нічия думка на {{deity_pronoun:тебе|Тебе}} не впливає, бо {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} не судиш людей за їхнім становищем.
uk.R: Вони послали до Ісуса кількох своїх учнів разом із людьми, які підтримували родину царя Ірода. Ті сказали: «Учителю, ми знаємо, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} чесний. Ми знаємо, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} правдиво навчаєш, як Бог хоче, щоб жили люди. Ти нікого не боїшся, бо до впливових людей {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} ставишся так само, як до всіх інших.

ja.L: そして彼らは、自分たちの弟子たちをヘロデ派の人々と一緒にイエスのところに遣わして言う。「先生、わたしたちは知っています。あなたは真実な方で、真理に基づいて神の道を教え、だれのことも気にかけられません。人の顔を見ないからです。
ja.B: 彼らは、自分たちの弟子をヘロデ派の人々と一緒にイエスのもとに遣わした。「先生」と彼らは言った。「わたしたちは、あなたが誠実な方で、真理をもって神の道を教えておられることを承知しています。あなたはだれにも左右されません。人の地位に目を留められないからです。
ja.R: 彼らは、自分たちの弟子の何人かを、イエスのところへ送りました。ヘロデ王の一族を支持するヘロデ派の人々も一緒でした。彼らは言いました。「先生、わたしたちは、あなたが正直な方だとよく知っています。神が望まれる生き方について、本当のことを教えておられます。あなたは、だれのことも恐れておられません。相手がどんなにえらい人でも、ほかの人と同じように扱われるからです。

decisions.choice: the Herodians: supporters of Herod's family, who ruled under Rome
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas ruled Galilee with Rome's approval. His supporters would favor the tax; many Pharisees resented it. The two groups were unlikely allies (Mark 3:6).

decisions.choice: look at the face of men: show favor because of a person's rank or appearance
decisions.reason: The law forbids judging by a person's standing (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 1:17). They praise Jesus for fearing no one, hoping he will answer rashly.

decisions.choice: true, in truth: honest, teaching what is really God's way
decisions.reason: Their words are flattery meant to set a trap (22:15, 18), yet what they say about Jesus is so.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: men who supported King Herod's family; the truth about the way God wants people to live
alternatives: the Herodians; the way of God in truth
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Herodians were and what "the way of God" means.

decisions.choice: truthful (B); honest (R)
decisions.reason: The adjective describes a person who speaks the truth. The noun "truth" later in the verse stays "truth" at every level.

decisions.choice: Maître; disciples at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:14: "Maître" is how French addresses a respected teacher, used for this address throughout the chapter. French keeps "disciples" at Readable, where English says "followers", as Mark's French does.

decisions.choice: wafuasi wa Herode (supporters of Herod)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of the Herodians (meaning decision m1). Swahili has no established word for the party, and "Maherodi" would read as several men named Herod.

decisions.choice: The questioners speak to Jesus in full 합쇼체 with honorifics, "저희" and "선생님" for "you", through 22:17
decisions.reason: Their flattery is the trap: they speak with full courtesy, as in the Korean Mark 12:14.

decisions.choice: "헤롯 당원들" (L, B), "헤롯 왕의 집안을 따르는 사람들" (R); "사람들의 얼굴을 보지 않다" (L), "사람의 지위를 따지지 않다" (B)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:13-14; Literal keeps the idiom of the face, which means showing favour by rank (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Present "보내며 말한다" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew's present tense of narration at Literal.

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy" and "Thầy" for "you" in the questioners' words, with no deity_pronoun span (22:16-17); "chúng tôi" for themselves
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:14: they address him as a teacher, flattering him, and Vietnamese then uses the same noun for "you"; a noun of address takes no setting (style guide section 6).

decisions.choice: "người thuộc phe Hê-rốt" (L, B); "người ủng hộ gia đình vua Hê-rốt" (R); "không nhìn mặt người ta" (L), "không xét người theo địa vị" (B)
decisions.reason: The wording of Mark 12:13-14. "Người ta" already takes in men and women, so the English people/men setting has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: tu (és, ensinas, te, olhas)
decisions.reason: The Pharisees' disciples and the Herodians speak to Jesus, so they use "tu", as everyone does who addresses him (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4). Their flattery and their trap (m3) show in what they say, not in the form of address.

decisions.choice: não olhas para o rosto das pessoas
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of the face; m2 explains it. Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "የሄሮድስ ወገኖች" (L, B); "የንጉሥ ሄሮድስን ቤተሰብ የሚደግፉ ሰዎች" (R)
decisions.reason: "ሄሮድሳውያን" is not a word most readers know; "የሄሮድስ ወገኖች" says they were Herod's party, and Readable explains it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "የሰዎችን" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span, as the English Literal
decisions.reason: "ሰዎች" already means people, men and women; Amharic has no traditional male-only wording of the same sense to offer as an alternative.

decisions.choice: "людей" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender span on "people|men"; Russian "люди" already means people in general, so the style guide gives it no span.

decisions.choice: "истина" (L, B); "правда" (R)
decisions.reason: Truth is a key term (style guide, section 6): "истина" at Literal and Balanced, the everyday "правда" at Readable.
The style guide's address for "Teacher" and its key term for truth. The Pharisees' men flatter Jesus but still say "आप".

decisions.choice: "मनुष्यों का मुँह नहीं देखते", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "people" or "men"; Hindi "मनुष्य" already means human beings of either sex. "मुँह देखना" is itself a Hindi idiom for showing favor, so Literal can keep the Greek picture.

decisions.choice: "людей" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is anthrōpos, and Ukrainian "люди" already includes men and women, so the English gender span has no Ukrainian counterpart.

decisions.choice: present "遣わして言う" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells this in the present tense; Literal keeps the Japanese present, Balanced and Readable narrate in the past. The same holds for 22:20-21.

decisions.choice: the questioners speak politely with respect forms ("教えておられる", "気にかけられません")
decisions.reason: Their praise is flattery meant to set a trap (m3). As in Mark 12:14, very courteous speech shows it and stands against the plain words of Jesus' reply.

decisions.choice: "人の顔", "人の地位" with no gender span (L, B)
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender span for people/men; Japanese "人" already means anyone.

decisions.choice: "ヘロデ王の一族を支持するヘロデ派の人々" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Herodians were (m1), as the English Readable does, and keeps the name used at the other levels.

source.text: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;

records.literal_gloss: Tell therefore us what to you seems: is it lawful to give poll tax to Caesar or not?

en.L: Tell us then, what do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think? Is it lawful to give [the] poll tax to Caesar, or not?"
en.B: So give us {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} opinion. Does the law permit paying the head tax to Caesar, or not?"
en.R: So tell us what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think. Does God's law allow us to pay taxes to Caesar, the Roman emperor? Or should we refuse?"

es.L: Dinos, pues, qué {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} parece: ¿es lícito dar [el] tributo personal al César, o no?».
es.B: Así que danos {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} opinión: ¿permite la ley pagar el tributo por persona al César, o no?».

sw.L: Basi tuambie, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unafikiri nini: je, ni halali kulipa kodi ya kichwa kwa Kaisari, au la?"

sw.R: Basi tuambie unafikiri nini. Je, sheria ya Mungu inaturuhusu kulipa kodi kwa Kaisari, mtawala mkuu wa Roma? Au tukatae?"

ko.L: 그러니 저희에게 말씀해 주십시오. 선생님께서는 어떻게 생각하십니까? 가이사에게 인두세를 바치는 것이 허락되어 있습니까, 아닙니까?"
ko.B: 그러니 선생님의 생각을 저희에게 말씀해 주십시오. 가이사에게 세금을 바치는 것이 율법에 맞습니까, 맞지 않습니까?"
ko.R: 그러니 선생님께서는 어떻게 생각하시는지 말씀해 주십시오. 하나님의 율법은 우리가 로마 황제 가이사에게 세금을 내도 된다고 합니까? 아니면 내지 말아야 합니까?"

pt.L: Dize-nos, então, o que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} parece: é lícito dar [o] imposto por pessoa a César, ou não?"

pt.R: Então, o que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} achas? A Lei de Deus permite que nós paguemos impostos a César, o imperador romano? Ou devemos nos recusar?"

am.L: እንግዲህ ምን እንደሚመስልህ ንገረን፤ ለቄሳር የነፍስ ግብር መስጠት ተፈቅዷል ወይስ አልተፈቀደም?»
am.B: ስለዚህ አስተያየትህን ንገረን። ለቄሳር የነፍስ ወከፍ ግብር መክፈል በሕግ የተፈቀደ ነው ወይስ አይደለም?»
am.R: ስለዚህ ምን እንደምታስብ ንገረን። የእግዚአብሔር ሕግ ለሮም ንጉሠ ነገሥት ለቄሳር ግብር እንድንከፍል ይፈቅድልናል? ወይስ እምቢ ማለት አለብን?»

ru.L: Итак, скажи нам, как {{deity_pronoun:тебе|Тебе}} кажется? Позволительно ли давать подушную подать кесарю или нет?»
ru.B: Так скажи нам своё мнение: позволяет ли Закон платить подушный налог кесарю или нет?»
ru.R: Так скажи нам, что {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} думаешь. Разрешает ли Божий Закон нам платить налоги кесарю, римскому императору? Или нам нужно отказаться?»

hi.L: तो हमें बताइए, आप क्या सोचते हैं? कैसर को कर देना उचित है या नहीं?"
hi.B: तो हमें अपनी राय दीजिए। क्या व्यवस्था के अनुसार कैसर को प्रति व्यक्ति कर देना ठीक है या नहीं?"
hi.R: तो हमें बताइए कि आप क्या सोचते हैं। क्या परमेश्वर की व्यवस्था हमें रोमी सम्राट कैसर को कर देने की अनुमति देती है? या हमें मना कर देना चाहिए?"

uk.L: Тож скажи нам, як {{deity_pronoun:тобі|Тобі}} здається: чи дозволено давати подушний податок кесареві, чи ні?»
uk.B: Тож скажи нам, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} про це думаєш. Чи дозволяє Закон платити подушне кесареві, чи ні?»
uk.R: Тож скажи нам, що {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} думаєш. Чи дозволяє Божий Закон платити податки кесареві, римському імператорові? Чи нам слід відмовитися?»

ja.L: それで、わたしたちに言ってください。あなたはどう思われますか？皇帝に人頭税を納めることは許されていますか、いませんか？」

ja.R: それで、教えてください。あなたはどう思われますか？ローマの皇帝に税金を納めることを、神の律法は許しているでしょうか？それとも、納めてはいけないのでしょうか？」

decisions.choice: poll tax: a yearly tax on each person, paid to Rome
decisions.reason: Rome took a tax on each person in Judea, paid in Roman coin. Many Jews hated it as a sign of foreign rule; a revolt broke out over it in AD 6 (Acts 5:37).

decisions.choice: Caesar: the Roman emperor, at this time Tiberius
decisions.reason: Caesar was the family name of the first emperors and became their title.

decisions.choice: is it lawful: allowed by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The question is whether paying a pagan ruler is right for God's people. "Yes" would anger the crowds; "no" would be rebellion against Rome.

decisions.choice: head tax (B); taxes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain word for a tax on each person. Readable keeps it general and explains Caesar.

decisions.choice: Or should we refuse?
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the other half of the question.

decisions.choice: tributo personal (L); tributo por persona (B); impuestos (R)
decisions.reason: The tax was paid by each person, a head tax (meaning decision m1); Spanish "impuesto por cabeza" is unusual, so Literal and Balanced say "personal" or "por persona".

decisions.choice: le cens (L); l’impôt par tête (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the Latin "census", the yearly tax on each person (m1); French has the same word, "le cens", which Literal keeps (and in 22:19). Balanced says plainly what it was; "tribut" would suggest a payment from a conquered people as a whole.

decisions.choice: "가이사" (L, B), "로마 황제 가이사" (R); "인두세" (L), "세금" (B, R); "허락되어 있다" (L), "율법에 맞다" (B)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:14: the Protestant name form, the poll tax named at Literal, and "lawful" meaning allowed by the law of Moses (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "thuế thân" (L, B), "thuế" (R); "Sê-sa", with "hoàng đế La Mã" added at R
decisions.reason: "Thuế thân" is the Vietnamese name for a tax levied on each person, the poll tax of the meaning decision; "Sê-sa" is the Protestant form of Mark 12:14.

decisions.choice: o imposto por pessoa
decisions.reason: The word names a yearly tax on each person (m1). "Tributo" is broader and "censo" now means only a population count, so Literal and Balanced say what the tax was; Readable keeps it general, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "የነፍስ ግብር" (L); "የነፍስ ወከፍ ግብር" (B); "ግብር" (R)
decisions.reason: The tax was a fixed sum on each person; "የነፍስ ወከፍ ግብር" says exactly that, and "ቀረጥ" would suggest a duty on goods.

decisions.choice: "कर" (L, R); "प्रति व्यक्ति कर" (B)
decisions.reason: The poll tax was a yearly tax on each person paid to Rome (meaning decision m1). Balanced says so; "जज़िया" would bring in a tax from Indian history.

decisions.choice: "人頭税" (L); "税金" (B, R); "皇帝", "ローマの皇帝" (R)
decisions.reason: The tax was paid by each person to Rome (m1). As in Mark 12:14, Literal names it and Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word; Caesar is "皇帝" (m2), and Readable adds "ローマの".

source.text: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Τί με πειράζετε, ὑποκριταί;

records.literal_gloss: Having known however Jesus the malice of them, said, Why me do you test, hypocrites?

en.L: But Jesus, knowing their malice, said, "Why are you testing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, hypocrites?
en.B: Jesus was aware of their malice. "You hypocrites," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "why are you putting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to the test?
en.R: But Jesus knew they were trying to do something evil. He said, "You are only pretending to be good! Why are you trying to trap {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Pero Jesús, conociendo la malicia de ellos, dijo: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} a prueba, hipócritas?
es.B: Jesús se dio cuenta de su malicia. «Hipócritas», dijo, «¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} a prueba?
es.R: Pero Jesús sabía que querían hacer algo malo. Les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes solo fingen|Vosotros solo fingís}} ser buenos! ¿Por qué {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} de atraparme?

fr.L: Mais Jésus, connaissant leur méchanceté, dit : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mettez-vous à l’épreuve, hypocrites ?
fr.B: Jésus vit bien leur malice. « Hypocrites, dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mettez-vous à l’épreuve ?
fr.R: Mais Jésus savait qu’ils voulaient faire quelque chose de mal. Il a dit : « Vous faites seulement semblant d’être bons ! Pourquoi essayez-vous de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} piéger ?

sw.L: Lakini Yesu, akiijua nia yao mbaya, alisema, "Kwa nini mnanijaribu, wanafiki?
sw.B: Yesu aliutambua ubaya wa nia yao, akasema, "Ninyi wanafiki, kwa nini mnanijaribu namna hii?
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alijua kwamba walitaka kufanya jambo baya. Akasema, "Mnajifanya tu kuwa watu wema! Kwa nini mnajaribu kuninasa?

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu biết sự gian ác của họ, nên nói: "Hỡi những kẻ đạo đức giả, sao các người thử {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu biết rõ ác ý của họ, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Hỡi những kẻ đạo đức giả, sao các người tìm cách gài bẫy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu biết họ đang muốn làm điều ác. Ngài nói: "Các người là những kẻ đạo đức giả! Sao các người tìm cách gài bẫy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 그들의 악한 속셈을 아시고 말씀하셨다. "위선자들아, 왜 나를 시험하느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 그들의 악한 속셈을 아시고 말씀하셨다. "위선자들아, 너희는 왜 나를 떠보느냐?
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 그들이 악한 일을 꾸미고 있다는 것을 아셨다. 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "너희 위선자들아! 왜 나를 속여 넘기려고 하느냐?

pt.L: Mas Jesus, conhecendo a malícia deles, disse: "Por que vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} põem à prova, hipócritas?
pt.B: Jesus percebeu a maldade deles. "Hipócritas", {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse, "por que vocês estão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pondo à prova?
pt.R: Mas Jesus sabia que eles queriam fazer uma coisa má. Ele disse: "Vocês só fingem ser bons! Por que estão tentando {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pegar numa armadilha?

am.L: ኢየሱስም ክፋታቸውን አውቆ እንዲህ አለ፦ «እናንተ ግብዞች፣ ለምን ትፈትኑኛላችሁ?
am.B: ኢየሱስ ክፋታቸውን ተረዳ። «እናንተ ግብዞች» አላቸው፤ «ለምን ትፈታተኑኛላችሁ?
am.R: ኢየሱስ ግን ክፉ ነገር ሊያደርጉ እንደሚሞክሩ አወቀ። እንዲህም አለ፦ «እናንተ ግብዞች! ጥሩ መስላችሁ ለመታየት ብቻ ታስመስላላችሁ። ለምን ልታጠምዱኝ ትሞክራላችሁ?

ru.L: Иисус же, узнав их лукавство, сказал: «Что {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} искушаете, лицемеры?
ru.B: Иисус понял их злой умысел. «Лицемеры», — сказал {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}, — «зачем вы {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} испытываете?
ru.R: Но Иисус знал, что они задумали недоброе. Он сказал: «Вы только притворяетесь хорошими! Зачем вы хотите поймать {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} в ловушку?

hi.L: पर यीशु ने उनकी दुष्टता जानकर कहा, "हे पाखंडियो, मुझे क्यों परखते हो?
hi.B: यीशु उनकी दुष्टता भाँप गए। "पाखंडियो," उन्होंने कहा, "तुम मुझे क्यों परख रहे हो?
hi.R: पर यीशु जान गए कि वे कुछ बुरा करने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं। उन्होंने कहा, "तुम बस अच्छे होने का दिखावा कर रहे हो! तुम मुझे फँसाने की कोशिश क्यों कर रहे हो?

uk.L: А Ісус, пізнавши їхню лукавість, сказав: «Чому {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} випробовуєте, лицеміри?
uk.B: Ісус бачив їхню злобу. «Лицеміри», — сказав {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}}, — «навіщо ви {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} випробовуєте?
uk.R: Але Ісус знав, що вони замислили зло. Він сказав: «Ви тільки вдаєте із себе добрих! Навіщо ви хочете {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} впіймати в пастку?

ja.L: しかしイエスは彼らの悪意を知って言われた。「偽善者たち、なぜわたしを試すのか？
ja.B: イエスは彼らの悪意に気づいておられた。「偽善者たち」とイエスは言われた。「なぜ、わたしを試そうとするのか？
ja.R: けれどもイエスは、彼らが悪いことをたくらんでいるのを知っておられました。イエスは言われました。「あなたたちは、善い人のふりをしているだけだ！なぜ、わたしをわなにかけようとするのか？

decisions.choice: test: try to catch him out
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the Pharisees' questions in 16:1, 19:3 and 22:35, and of the devil in 4:1.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people whose words hide their real aims
decisions.reason: Their praise in 22:16 covered a trap. The word first meant an actor.

decisions.choice: You are only pretending to be good
decisions.reason: As in 7:5, Readable says what a hypocrite does.

decisions.choice: "위선자들" at every level
decisions.reason: The settled word in the Korean Matthew (6:2, 15:7); the English Readable's explanation is carried by the context, as in the Korean Matthew 15:7.

decisions.choice: "시험하다" (L); "떠보다" (B); "속여 넘기려고 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The sense is trying to catch him out (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable as in the Korean Mark 12:15.

decisions.choice: "những kẻ đạo đức giả" at every level; "các người" for the questioners (22:18-21)
decisions.reason: The settled Matthew word for hypocrites (6:2; 15:7); Jesus speaks to opponents as "các người".

decisions.choice: "እናንተ ግብዞች!" with the explanation after it (R)
alternatives: the explanation alone, as the English Readable
decisions.reason: "ግብዝ" is a plain everyday word in Amharic, so Readable keeps it and adds the English Readable's explanation beside it.

decisions.choice: "पाखंडियो" (L, B); "तुम बस अच्छे होने का दिखावा कर रहे हो" (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's word for the address; Readable says what a hypocrite does, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "偽善者" (L, B); "善い人のふりをしているだけだ" (R)
decisions.reason: A hypocrite's words hide his real aims (m2). Readable says what a hypocrite does, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: denarius: a Roman silver coin, a day's wage for a laborer
decisions.reason: A vineyard worker is paid a denarius for a day's work in 20:2.

decisions.choice: units setting for the denarius
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman coin's name. Balanced and Readable describe it, with denarius as the setting's alternative.

decisions.choice: {{units:una moneda de plata que valía el salario de un día|un denario}}
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say what the coin was worth, a day's wage (meaning decision m1), with the coin's name as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

decisions.choice: {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku moja|dinari}}
decisions.reason: As in English and as in John 6:7: Balanced and Readable say what the coin was worth, a day's wage (meaning decision m1), with "dinari" as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

decisions.choice: {{units:하루 품삯인 은화 한 닢|데나리온 한 닢}} (B); {{units:일꾼이 하루 일하고 받는 은화 한 닢|데나리온 한 닢}} (R); Literal keeps "데나리온"
decisions.reason: The same spans as the Korean Mark 12:15: the value by default, the coin's name as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "một đơ-ni-ê" (L, and the alternative at B, R); its worth as a day's wage by default (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:15 and Matthew 18:28: "đơ-ni-ê" is the Protestant transliteration of the Roman coin; the setting gives its worth, as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{units:የአንድ ቀን ደመወዝ የሚያህል የብር ሳንቲም|አንድ ዲናር}} (B)
decisions.reason: A coin has no metric form, so the Amharic follows the English span: the default says what the coin was worth, and the Measures setting shows its name, "ዲናር". Literal keeps the coin.

decisions.choice: {{units:серебряную монету, равную дневному заработку|денарий}}
decisions.reason: A coin has no metric form, so the units setting describes its worth by default and gives the coin as the alternative, as the English does. Literal keeps the denarius.

decisions.choice: {{units:चाँदी का एक सिक्का, जो एक दिन की मज़दूरी के बराबर था|एक दीनार}} (B); {{units:चाँदी का एक सिक्का, जितना एक मज़दूर एक दिन में कमाता है|एक दीनार}} (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable describe the coin and its worth by default, with the denarius as the alternative; Literal keeps the coin's name.

decisions.choice: {{units:一日分の賃金にあたる銀貨|デナリオン銀貨}} (B, R); "デナリオン" (L)
decisions.reason: As in the English and in Mark 12:15, the units setting gives the coin's worth, a day's wage (m1), by default and its name as the alternative; Literal keeps the coin.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Whose image this and the inscription?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Whose image [is] this, and [whose] inscription?"
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Whose portrait is this? And whose title is written on it?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "Whose picture is on this coin? Whose name is written on it?"

es.L: Y les dice: «¿De quién [es] esta imagen, y [de quién] la inscripción?».
es.B: Entonces les preguntó: «¿De quién es este retrato? ¿Y de quién es el título que lleva escrito?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿De quién es la cara que está en esta moneda? ¿De quién es el nombre que tiene escrito?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « De qui [est] cette image, et [de qui] l’inscription ? »
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « De qui est ce portrait ? Et de qui est le titre inscrit dessus ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé : « De qui est le portrait sur cette pièce ? De qui est le nom écrit dessus ? »

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Ya nani picha hii na maandishi?"
sw.B: Kisha akawauliza, "Sura hii ni ya nani? Na maandishi haya ya cheo ni ya nani?"
sw.R: Yesu akawauliza, "Picha iliyo kwenye sarafu hii ni ya nani? Na jina lililoandikwa juu yake ni la nani?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Hình này và dòng chữ [này] là của ai?"
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Đây là hình mặt của ai? Và danh hiệu của ai được khắc trên đó?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi họ: "Hình trên đồng tiền này là của ai? Và tên của ai được khắc trên đó?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "이 형상과 글자는 누구의 것이냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "이 얼굴은 누구의 얼굴이고, 여기 새겨진 글자는 누구의 이름이냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "이 동전에 있는 얼굴은 누구 얼굴이냐? 여기 쓰여 있는 이름은 누구 이름이냐?"

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes diz: "De quem [é] esta imagem e [de quem é] a inscrição?"
pt.B: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes perguntou: "De quem é este retrato? E de quem é o título escrito nela?"
pt.R: Jesus perguntou a eles: "De quem é a figura que está nesta moeda? De quem é o nome escrito nela?"

am.L: ይላቸዋል፦ «ይህ መልክና ይህ ጽሕፈት የማን ነው?»
am.B: እርሱም «ይህ የማን መልክ ነው? በላዩስ የተጻፈው የማን ማዕረግ ነው?» ብሎ ጠየቃቸው።
am.R: ኢየሱስም «በዚህ ሳንቲም ላይ ያለው የማን ምስል ነው? በላዩስ የተጻፈው የማን ስም ነው?» ብሎ ጠየቃቸው።

ru.L: И говорит им: «Чьё это изображение и [чья] надпись?»
ru.B: Тогда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} спросил их: «Чьё это изображение? И чей титул здесь написан?»
ru.R: Иисус спросил их: «Чьё лицо на этой монете? Чьё имя на ней написано?»

hi.L: और [यीशु] उनसे कहते हैं, "यह छवि और लेख किसका [है]?"
hi.B: तब उन्होंने उनसे पूछा, "यह चेहरा किसका है? और इस पर किसकी उपाधि लिखी है?"
hi.R: यीशु ने उनसे पूछा, "इस सिक्के पर किसकी तस्वीर है? इस पर किसका नाम लिखा है?"

uk.L: І каже {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} їм: «Чиє це зображення і [чий] напис?»
uk.B: Тоді {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} запитав їх: «Чиє це обличчя? І чий титул тут написаний?»
uk.R: Ісус запитав їх: «Чиє зображення на цій монеті? Чиє імʼя на ній написане?»

ja.L: すると[イエスは]彼らに言われる。「これはだれの像で、[だれの]銘か？」
ja.B: イエスは彼らに尋ねられた。「これはだれの顔か？それに、ここに書いてあるのはだれの名か？」
ja.R: イエスは彼らに聞かれました。「この銀貨には、だれの顔がきざまれている？それに、だれの名前が書いてある？」

decisions.choice: image and inscription: the emperor's head and his titles
decisions.reason: The denarius of Tiberius bore his head and an inscription naming him son of the divine Augustus. Many Jews found such coins offensive.

decisions.choice: image: perhaps an echo of people made in God's image (Genesis 1:27)
decisions.reason: The word is the one the Greek Old Testament uses in Genesis 1:26-27. If the coin bearing Caesar's image belongs to Caesar, what bears God's image belongs to God. Jesus does not say this outright.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: "형상" (L); "얼굴" (B, R) for eikon
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that may echo people made in God's image (meaning decision), as in the Korean Mark 12:16.

decisions.choice: Present "말씀하신다" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew's present tense of narration at Literal.

decisions.choice: "መልክ" (L, B); "ምስል" (R)
decisions.reason: "መልክ" is the likeness of a face, the word Amharic uses for being made in God's image, so Literal and Balanced keep the possible echo the meaning decision notes; Readable says picture.

The word is an image or likeness, here the emperor's head (m1). Literal keeps "像", which leaves room for the possible echo of God's image (m2); Balanced and Readable say what was on the coin, as in Mark 12:16.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, Caesar's.

en.L: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Caesar's."
en.B: "Caesar's," they answered.
en.R: They answered, "Caesar's."

es.L: Le dicen: «Del César».
es.B: «Del César», respondieron.
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Del César».

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « De César. »
fr.B: « De César », répondirent-ils.
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « De César. »

sw.L: Wanamwambia, "Ya Kaisari."
sw.B: "Ya Kaisari," wakajibu.
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Ni ya Kaisari."

vi.L: Họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Của Sê-sa."
vi.B: Họ đáp: "Của Sê-sa."
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Của Sê-sa."

ko.L: 그들이 그분께 말한다. "가이사의 것입니다."
ko.B: 그들이 "가이사의 것입니다" 하고 대답했다.
ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. "가이사의 것입니다. 로마 황제의 것입니다."

pt.L: Eles {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizem: "De César."
pt.B: "De César", responderam eles.
pt.R: Eles responderam: "De César."

am.L: ይሉታል፦ «የቄሳር።»
am.B: «የቄሳር ነው» ብለው መለሱለት።
am.R: እነርሱም «የቄሳር ነው» ብለው መለሱ።

ru.L: Говорят {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}: «Кесаря.»
ru.B: «Кесаря», — ответили они.
ru.R: Они ответили: «Кесаря.»

hi.L: वे उनसे कहते हैं, "कैसर का।"
hi.B: "कैसर का," उन्होंने उत्तर दिया।
hi.R: उन्होंने जवाब दिया, "कैसर का।"

uk.L: Кажуть {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Кесареве.»
uk.B: «Кесареве», — відповіли вони.
uk.R: Вони відповіли: «Кесареве.»

ja.L: 彼らはイエスに言う。「皇帝のです。」
ja.B: 「皇帝のです」と彼らは答えた。
ja.R: 彼らは答えました。「ローマの皇帝のです。」

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Then he says to them, Give back therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar and the things of God to God.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Give back then the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God."
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Then pay Caesar what you owe Caesar, and pay God what you owe God."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "So pay back to Caesar what is his. And pay back to God what is God's."

es.L: Entonces les dice: «{{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}}, pues, lo del César al César, y lo de Dios a Dios».
es.B: Y les dijo: «Pues entonces, lo que le {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} al César, {{plural_you:páguenselo|pagádselo}} al César, y lo que le {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} a Dios, {{plural_you:páguenselo|pagádselo}} a Dios».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Entonces {{plural_you:devuélvanle|devolvedle}} al César lo que es suyo. Y {{plural_you:devuélvanle|devolvedle}} a Dios lo que es de Dios».

fr.L: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Rendez donc les choses de César à César, et les choses de Dieu à Dieu. »
fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Payez donc à César ce que vous devez à César, et à Dieu ce que vous devez à Dieu. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Alors rendez à César ce qui est à lui. Et rendez à Dieu ce qui est à Dieu. »

sw.L: Kisha anawaambia, "Basi mrudishieni Kaisari vya Kaisari, na Mungu vya Mungu."
sw.B: Naye akawaambia, "Basi, kile mnachodaiwa na Kaisari mlipeni Kaisari, na kile mnachodaiwa na Mungu mlipeni Mungu."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Basi mrudishieni Kaisari kilicho chake. Na mrudishieni Mungu kilicho cha Mungu."

vi.L: Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Vậy hãy trả lại cho Sê-sa các thứ của Sê-sa, và cho Đức Chúa Trời các thứ của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Vậy thì hãy trả cho Sê-sa những gì thuộc về Sê-sa, và trả cho Đức Chúa Trời những gì thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Vậy hãy trả cho Sê-sa những gì thuộc về ông ấy. Và hãy trả cho Đức Chúa Trời những gì thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 그때에 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "그러면 가이사의 것들은 가이사에게 돌려주고, 하나님의 것들은 하나님께 [돌려드려라]."
ko.B: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 가이사에게 갚을 것은 가이사에게 갚고, 하나님께 드릴 것은 하나님께 드려라."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 가이사의 것은 가이사에게 돌려주어라. 그리고 하나님의 것은 하나님께 돌려드려라."

pt.L: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes diz: "Devolvam, pois, as coisas de César a César, e as coisas de Deus a Deus."
pt.B: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Então paguem a César o que vocês devem a César, e paguem a Deus o que vocês devem a Deus."
pt.R: Jesus disse a eles: "Então devolvam a César o que é dele. E devolvam a Deus o que é de Deus."

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ ይላቸዋል፦ «እንግዲያውስ የቄሳርን ለቄሳር፣ የእግዚአብሔርንም ለእግዚአብሔር መልሱ።»
am.B: እርሱም «እንግዲያውስ ለቄሳር የሚገባውን ለቄሳር ክፈሉ፤ ለእግዚአብሔርም የሚገባውን ለእግዚአብሔር ክፈሉ» አላቸው።
am.R: ኢየሱስም «እንግዲያውስ የቄሳርን ለቄሳር መልሱ። የእግዚአብሔር የሆነውንም ለእግዚአብሔር መልሱ» አላቸው።

ru.L: Тогда говорит им: «Отдайте же кесарево кесарю и Божье Богу.»
ru.B: И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сказал им: «Тогда отдайте кесарю то, что вы должны кесарю, и Богу то, что вы должны Богу.»
ru.R: Иисус сказал им: «Так верните кесарю то, что принадлежит ему. И верните Богу то, что принадлежит Богу.»

hi.L: तब [यीशु] उनसे कहते हैं, "इसलिए जो कैसर का है, वह कैसर को लौटा दो, और जो परमेश्वर का है, वह परमेश्वर को।"
hi.B: और उन्होंने उनसे कहा, "तो जो तुम्हें कैसर का देना है, वह कैसर को चुकाओ, और जो परमेश्वर का देना है, वह परमेश्वर को चुकाओ।"
hi.R: यीशु ने उनसे कहा, "तो जो कैसर का है, वह कैसर को लौटा दो। और जो परमेश्वर का है, वह परमेश्वर को लौटा दो।"

uk.L: Тоді каже {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} їм: «Тож віддайте кесареве кесареві, а Боже — Богові.»
uk.B: І {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав їм: «Тоді віддайте кесареві те, що ви винні кесареві, а Богові — те, що ви винні Богові.»
uk.R: Ісус сказав їм: «Тож віддайте кесареві те, що належить йому. І віддайте Богові те, що належить Богові.»

ja.L: そのときイエスは彼らに言われる。「それでは、皇帝のものは皇帝に、神のものは神に返しなさい。」
ja.B: するとイエスは言われた。「それなら、皇帝に属するものは皇帝に返し、神に属するものは神に返しなさい。」
ja.R: イエスは彼らに言われました。「それなら、皇帝のものは、皇帝に返しなさい。そして、神のものは、神に返しなさい。」

decisions.choice: give back: pay what is owed
decisions.reason: The verb differs from "give" in their question (22:17). It means to pay back a debt. The coin already belongs to Caesar.

decisions.choice: the things of God: all that belongs to God, the people themselves included
decisions.reason: The answer neither forbids the tax nor puts Caesar on God's level. If the coin bears Caesar's image, people bear God's (Genesis 1:27), and owe him themselves. The second half has the greater weight.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: pay what you owe (B); pay back (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that this is a debt being paid.

decisions.choice: devuelvan (L, R); lo que le deben ... páguenselo (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is "give back", pay what is owed (meaning decision m1), not simply "give" as they had asked in verse 17. Literal and Readable say "devolver"; Balanced spells out the debt, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mrudishieni (L, R); mnachodaiwa ... mlipeni (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is "give back", pay what is owed (meaning decision m1), not simply "give". Literal and Readable say "kurudishia"; Balanced spells out the debt, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "돌려주다" / "[돌려드려라]" (L, R); "갚다" / "드리다" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means paying back what is owed (meaning decision); the honorific "드리다" is used toward God. Literal brackets the second verb the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: "trả lại" (L); "trả" (B, R) for "give back"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:17: the verb means paying what is owed (meaning decision), and the same verb is kept for God so the two halves of the saying stay parallel.

decisions.choice: Devolvam (L, R); paguem ... o que vocês devem (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pay back what is owed (m1), unlike "dar" in their question (22:17), so Literal and Readable say "devolver" and Balanced names the debt.

decisions.choice: "መልሱ" (give back) (L, R); "ክፈሉ" (pay) (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is to give back what is owed, not simply to give; "መልሱ" keeps that, and Balanced says pay what is due.

decisions.choice: "віддайте"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:17: the Greek verb means to pay back what is owed; "віддати" in Ukrainian carries both giving and paying a debt, while "повернути" would suggest the coin was borrowed.

decisions.choice: "返しなさい" (every level)
decisions.reason: They asked about giving; Jesus answers with a verb for paying back what is owed (m1). "返す" keeps that turn at every level, as in Mark 12:17, where "納める" would only repeat their word.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν, καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard they marveled, and having left him they went away.

en.L: And hearing [this], they marveled, and they left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and went away.
en.B: His answer astonished them, and they went off and left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone.
en.R: They were amazed at what Jesus said. So they left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and went away.

es.L: Y oyendo [esto], se maravillaron, y dejándolo, se fueron.
es.B: Su respuesta los dejó asombrados; {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejaron en paz y se fueron.
es.R: Se quedaron admirados de lo que Jesús dijo. Así que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejaron y se fueron.

fr.L: Et, ayant entendu [cela], ils furent étonnés, et, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissant, ils s’en allèrent.
fr.B: Sa réponse les remplit d’étonnement ; ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissèrent et s’en allèrent.
fr.R: Ils ont été très étonnés par ce que Jésus avait dit. Alors ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont laissé et ils sont partis.

sw.L: Na wakisikia [hayo], walishangaa, na wakimwacha, waliondoka.
sw.B: Jibu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} liliwashangaza, nao wakamwacha, wakaondoka.
sw.R: Walishangazwa na maneno ya Yesu. Basi wakamwacha, wakaondoka.

vi.L: Và nghe [vậy], họ kinh ngạc, rồi bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà đi.
vi.B: Nghe câu trả lời ấy, họ rất kinh ngạc, rồi để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại mà bỏ đi.
vi.R: Họ rất ngạc nhiên về câu trả lời của Đức Giê-xu. Vì thế họ để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại và bỏ đi.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 [이 말씀을] 듣고 놀랐다. 그리고 그분을 버려두고 떠나갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 이 말씀을 듣고 놀랐다. 그리고 예수를 남겨 두고 떠나갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 예수의 대답을 듣고 무척 놀랐다. 그래서 예수를 그냥 두고 가 버렸다.

pt.L: E, ouvindo [isso], ficaram admirados e, deixando-{{deity_pronoun:o|O}}, foram embora.
pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} resposta os deixou espantados, e eles foram embora e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} deixaram em paz.
pt.R: Eles ficaram admirados com o que Jesus disse. Por isso {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} deixaram e foram embora.

am.L: ሰምተውም ተደነቁ፤ ትተውትም ሄዱ።
am.B: በመልሱም እጅግ ተደነቁ፤ ትተውትም ሄዱ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ በተናገረው ነገር ተገረሙ። ስለዚህ ትተውት ሄዱ።

ru.L: И, услышав, они удивились и, оставив {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, ушли.
ru.B: Его ответ изумил их, и они ушли, оставив {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} в покое.
ru.R: Они были поражены тем, что сказал Иисус. И они оставили {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} и ушли.

hi.L: और [यह] सुनकर वे अचंभित हुए, और उन्हें छोड़कर चले गए।
hi.B: उनका उत्तर सुनकर वे दंग रह गए, और उन्हें छोड़कर चले गए।
hi.R: यीशु की बात सुनकर वे हैरान रह गए। इसलिए वे उन्हें छोड़कर चले गए।

uk.L: І, почувши [це], вони здивувалися і, залишивши {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, пішли.
uk.B: Його відповідь їх вразила, і вони залишили {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} й пішли геть.
uk.R: Їх здивувало те, що сказав Ісус. Тож вони залишили {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} і пішли.

ja.L: そして彼らは[これを]聞いて驚き、イエスを残して立ち去った。
ja.B: 彼らはこの答えを聞いて驚嘆し、イエスを残して去って行った。
ja.R: 彼らは、イエスの答えにとても驚きました。そして、イエスを残して帰って行きました。

decisions.choice: marveled: were amazed, though not won over
decisions.reason: They have no reply, so they leave. Amazement in Matthew does not always mean belief (8:27; 27:14).

decisions.choice: [이 말씀을] (L)
decisions.reason: Korean "듣다" needs an object.
